items.title: Israeli far-right minister Smotrich says ICC seeks his arrest
items.description: Smotrich is the third Israeli official targeted by the ICC, after Netanyahu and Gallant, for war crimes in Gaza.

items.title: Czechia: Uproar over Sudeten German gathering in Brno
items.description: The first gathering of Sudeten Germans in Czechia since World War II is set to go ahead this weekend despite a political backlash that has exposed tensions over one of Central Europe's most painful historical legacies.

items.description: US bureau chief Jacob Magid discusses details of Iran negotiations, an emboldened Hamas in Gaza and initial results from Fatah central committee elections The post Daily Briefing May 19: Trump frustrated as Iran talks stall, Gulf wary of renewed war appeared first on The Times of Israel.

items.title: Trump says holding off on strike on Iran at request of Gulf allies
items.description: After issuing thinly veiled threats against Iran over the weekend, US President Trump appeared to strike a different tone on May 18. He described ongoing peace talks with Tehran as “very positive” and even claimed he had paused a planned US military strike.

items.title: Russia’s Hospitals Overwhelmed as War Wounded Flood Civilian Clinics
items.description: Russian military hospitals in Russia are reportedly overwhelmed by wounded soldiers from the war in Ukraine, forcing civilian hospitals to be repurposed for military use. Reports describe worsening access to care for ordinary patients and widespread strain on healthcare systems amid rising casualties and resource short…

items.title: As Israeli elections approach, the opposition focuses on rejecting Netanyahu rather than defining peace
items.description: Even as the current prime minister's coalition appears to be in deep trouble, most of his rivals have not dared to break with his nationalist rhetoric, and seem trapped in a conceptual dead end when it comes to coexistence with Palestinians – whether Israeli citizens, residents of Gaza, or the West Bank.

items.title: Tested by Iran war, Qatar is still faithful to its core mission: Mediation
items.description: Before the war, Qatar had built itself into a diplomatic power by mediating disputes near and far. Hit hard by Iran, the tiny Persian Gulf country is not wavering in that mission, seen as central to its identity. Still, it recognizes it has security needs, too.

items.title: World News in Brief: More attacks in Ukraine, violence against children in Haiti, refugee IDs in Africa
items.description: Civilians, including humanitarians, continue to face great danger across war-torn Ukraine amid ongoing hostilities, according to the UN humanitarian relief coordination office there, OCHA.

items.title: Ukrainian Drone Attack Kills 2 in Belgorod Region
items.description: Officials said the attack took place in the village of Borisovka, located north of the border with eastern Ukraine’s Kharkiv region.

items.title: Ukraine launches large-scale drone strikes on Russia
items.description: As peace talks stall, Ukraine launches one of the biggest drone strikes against Russia since the beginning of Russia's full-scale invasion in an attempt to weaken Russia's war machine.

items.title: Inside the 'kill-zone' on Ukraine's front line, where new weapons have transformed war
items.description: Machines are increasingly replacing humans on the front line, but troops are still vital for defending territory.

items.title: 'The Strike Hit Right Above Us': A Night Under Russian Bombs In Dobropillya
items.description: Russia is preparing to assault the city of Dobropillya, according to Ukraine’s military. Located a few kilometers from the front line, the city is burning and being destroyed by bombs, artillery, and drones. Despite daily shelling, some civilians flatly refuse to leave and remain in Dobropillya.
